problem.title: Problem
problem.subtitle: What challenge was this project built to solve?
problem.content:
To'rtko'l needed an all-in-one app combining taxi, food delivery, handyman services, and store shopping in one place, so users wouldn't need to visit separate platforms for each service.

Developing separate apps for iOS and Android and publishing them to app stores takes a lot of time, and users would also have to download and install them. Therefore, the decision was made to build a web application that opens directly inside Telegram, which people already use every day.

role.title: My Role
role.subtitle: Key responsibilities and engineering contributions
role.content:
I was one of 2 frontend developers on the project. I mainly built the following:
• SMS OTP Login (AuthPage): phone number entry, 5-digit verification code, session handling, and new user onboarding. The file was 100% written by me.
• Taxi booking screen (Taxi component): tariff tier selection (Comfort, Ekonom) and bottom order sheet. At this stage, it was UI-only without backend and map integration.
• RTK Query auth service and Redux slice (authApi, authSlice): token management and TypeScript types.
• Restaurant details page (RestaurantDetail): categories and food menu listings, mostly authored by me.

We collaborated closely with my teammate on language selection, user profile, promo codes, and cart pages.

team.title: Team
team.subtitle: Team composition and collaboration workflow
team.content:
We were a 3-person team on the project: 1 backend developer using Python, and 2 frontend developers (myself and my teammate). We split the frontend work into domain modules: I built authentication, taxi, and restaurant pages, while my teammate handled the home screen and common components.

Work was managed on GitHub via feature branches and pull requests, with no direct commits to main. From December 2025 to February 2026, 8 PRs were merged. We integrated with the backend over REST API contracts.

decisions.title: Technical Decisions
decisions.subtitle: Architecture, tech stack, and tool choices
decisions.stack_content: React 19, TypeScript 5.9, and Vite 7. Styling powered by Tailwind CSS v4, animations by Framer Motion.
decisions.state_content: Server data (restaurants, menus, banners, branches, services) is fetched via Redux Toolkit and RTK Query. The auth token is stored in localStorage, while authSlice manages runtime session state. This approach is simple but vulnerable to XSS. A more secure alternative is httpOnly cookies, which requires backend adjustments.
decisions.why_rtk_content: To avoid manually handling loading and error states for each request and prevent redundant re-fetching of identical data (caching). I authored the auth service (authApi) here.

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.subtitle: Engineering obstacles faced and how they were solved
challenges.content:
1. SMS OTP authentication flow: This was a two-step process where the phone number is submitted, the backend returns a session token, and the user enters a 5-digit verification code verified against that session. New users are routed to a registration step. The main challenge was preserving the phone number and session state between steps, disabling submit buttons until the code is fully entered, and preventing duplicate requests during in-flight network calls.

2. Blank screens on network delays: To prevent empty screens while fetching initial data, loading skeletons were implemented across the home page, restaurant listings, shops, and service catalogues.

3. Incomplete modules: At this stage, the taxi booking and shopping cart screens remained UI-only prototypes without active backend integration. Errors were primarily displayed using basic feedback messages, with dedicated empty-state and error-state screens deferred to subsequent milestones.

results.title: Results
results.subtitle: Project outcomes, metrics, and business impact
results.content:
• Core frontend delivered: SMS OTP authentication, restaurants and menus, branch-specific services, and promo banners successfully integrated with a live backend.
• Screens and bottom navigation ready for taxi, shops, and handyman services. Taxi and cart remained UI-only at this milestone.
• Zero installation friction: Users open and access the application seamlessly inside Telegram.
